homePage.metaDescription: A public record rooted in heritage, systems, dignity, and the strengths of autistic and neurodivergent communities.
homePage.title: We ARE the Spectrum.
homePage.lead: Spectrum of Strengths is building a public record rooted in dignity, heritage, and the strengths of neurodivergent communities, including autistic and ADHD people.
homePage.intro: We celebrate history and tradition, identify gaps boldly, and explore evidence-led products and changes that bridge unmet needs and create shared value.
homePage.valuesTitle: Four ways of thinking about value
homePage.valuesIntro: These four ideas guide how we look at needs, solutions, and shared benefit.
homePage.captureBody: Recognize and share the economic and social benefits created by people’s knowledge, work, and relationships, so value reaches the communities who help create it and supports lasting work.
homePage.transformationBody: Improve existing knowledge, services, relationships, or resources so they work better for people and communities.
homePage.creationBody: Develop new ideas, tools, products, or services in response to a real need.
homePage.preservationBody: Protect useful knowledge, practices, and relationships so they can continue to benefit people over time.
homePage.methodTitle: From a need to shared value
homePage.methodIntro: Our living lab will connect evidence of a need with a proposed response and the value it could create. These are questions to examine, not promised outcomes.
homePage.needBody: Document the gap, who it affects, and the evidence behind it.
homePage.responseBody: Describe a product, service, or practical change that could bridge the gap.
homePage.benefitBody: Explain the possible social benefit and economic return, including who could receive and sustain that value.
homePage.recordBody: The archive and journal will grow as research, lived experience, historical material, and organizational progress are prepared for publication. Building trust with national bodies and professionals takes time; we will share confirmed milestones when they are ready for the public record. This first stage sets the direction and does not claim that services or programs are already operating.
homePage.developmentBody: Events, contact options, volunteering, and donations are for later stages. None are active through this site yet; details will be added when they are ready to share.

foundationsPage.metaDescription: Explore the origins, purpose, contributors, and founding direction of Spectrum of Strengths.
foundationsPage.title: Foundations
foundationsPage.intro: This page sets out the founding direction. It can grow as contributors, evidence, and historical records are confirmed.
foundationsPage.originsBody: The starting point is a belief that heritage, history, and tradition hold knowledge that can help shape better systems today. The archive will document sources and stories as they are gathered and approved for publication.
foundationsPage.purposeBody: We aim to celebrate strengths, identify unmet social needs and institutional gaps, and explore products and practical changes that meet needs, create shared value, and benefit neurodivergent communities, including autistic and ADHD people, and the wider systems around them.
foundationsPage.contributorsBody: Contributor and partner profiles will be added when names, roles, and descriptions are confirmed and approved for sharing.
foundationsPage.relationshipsBody: We are focusing first on the relationships and due process needed to establish this work in Canada. We intend to take the time needed to build trust with national bodies and professionals before describing joint work publicly. Cross-border work remains a later intention. The journal will distinguish conversations and plans from confirmed commitments, with dates and source context when available.
foundationsPage.embodimentBody: We put the purpose into practice by connecting evidence and lived experience with ways to create, transform, preserve, and fairly share value.

archivePage.metaDescription: A growing public journal of heritage, research, lived experience, social needs, and organizational progress.
archivePage.title: Archive & journal
archivePage.intro: A living record with heritage and systems as its anchor, connecting histories, research, experiences, needs, ideas, and progress.
archivePage.heritageBody: Historical records and traditions that help explain how systems have developed.
archivePage.researchBody: Research and documented evidence related to social needs and possible responses.
archivePage.experienceBody: Experiences and perspectives shared with permission and presented with care.
archivePage.gapsBody: Examples of unmet needs, the systems around them, and ideas for products or changes that bridge the gaps and create shared value.
archivePage.progressBody: Dated updates on plans, relationship building, work in progress, and confirmed milestones. Private correspondence can be cited without publishing the full message.
archivePage.entriesIntro: Entries will celebrate strengths and show the path from evidence to action. When there is enough information to share, a documented need, proposed response, and potential shared value will appear together. Plans and correspondence will be dated without treating them as completed work.
archivePage.emptyTitle: The journal is just getting started
archivePage.emptyBody: No journal entries have been published yet. Entries will appear here as research, experiences, and records are prepared for public sharing.
archivePage.dateNote: Entries will include publication dates and source context when available.

entries.title: Spectrum of Strengths opens its public record
entries.summary: Spectrum of Strengths is opening a public record rooted in heritage, history, tradition, dignity, and the strengths of neurodivergent communities, including autistic and ADHD people. We intend to bring research and lived experience together in an archive and living lab, identify unmet needs, and develop practical responses that create and share value. Our plans include products and future community centres. These are intentions under development; no community centres or programs are currently operating.

glossaryPage.metaDescription: Plain-language definitions of heritage, systems, dignity, gap bridging, and the four value principles.
glossaryPage.title: Key terms
glossaryPage.intro: These working definitions explain terms that have a particular meaning in our approach. They can be refined as the framework develops.
glossaryPage.heritageBody: Knowledge, histories, practices, and traditions carried forward by people and communities.
glossaryPage.leadershipBody: Setting a direction that looks ahead, recognizes needs, and brings people and resources together to make change possible.
glossaryPage.systemsBody: The structures, relationships, and practices that shape how support and opportunity reach people.
glossaryPage.gapFindingBody: Identifying where people’s needs are not being met, using evidence and lived experience to understand what is missing.
glossaryPage.gapBridgingBody: Connecting an identified need to a practical response, service, product, or change in a system.
glossaryPage.captureBody: Making sure that benefits created through knowledge, work, and relationships are recognized and shared fairly.
glossaryPage.transformationBody: Changing existing resources, practices, or services so that they provide greater benefit.
glossaryPage.creationBody: Developing something useful in response to a need, such as an idea, tool, product, or service.
glossaryPage.preservationBody: Keeping valuable knowledge, practices, and relationships available for future use.
glossaryPage.livingLabBody: An ongoing way of learning from real experiences and evidence while ideas and responses are being developed.

developmentsPage.eventsBody: Public events and registration are not part of this first stage. Information will be posted when plans are confirmed.
developmentsPage.contactBody: Contact options are in development. This page does not accept or send messages.

privacyPage.metaDescription: How the Spectrum of Strengths website currently handles submissions, external websites, and GitHub Pages hosting.
privacyPage.intro: This page summarizes how the website currently works. It will be updated before new ways of submitting information or other data practices are introduced.
privacyPage.submissionsBody: The current site does not provide working contact, newsletter, event registration, or payment forms. It does not ask visitors to submit those kinds of personal information.
privacyPage.externalBody: Some links may lead to external websites. Those sites have their own privacy and content practices.
privacyPage.languagesBody: Core site content is offered in English and French. External resources may be available only in the language used by their publishers.
privacyPage.detailsBody: This site is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub says it logs visitors’ IP addresses for security. Spectrum of Strengths does not use a visitor analytics service on this site.
privacyPage.detailsLinkLabel: Read GitHub Pages’ data collection information

accessibilityPage.metaDescription: Learn about the accessibility features considered in the Spectrum of Strengths website and its review status.
accessibilityPage.intro: The site uses clear headings, keyboard navigation, a skip link, responsive layouts, and reduced-motion preferences.
accessibilityPage.motionTitle: Motion on the Home and archive pages
accessibilityPage.motionBody: The value ideas on Home and the archive themes each change automatically about every 6 seconds with a gentle fade. Rotation pauses while your pointer is over a carousel and resumes when it leaves. Keyboard focus stops rotation until you use the play control. Use the small controls to pause, play, or move between ideas. If your device is set to reduce motion, each carousel is replaced by a static layout showing all its ideas.
accessibilityPage.reviewBody: Automated accessibility checks and the organization's manual review have been completed. The organization reported no actionable high or medium findings. Accessibility feedback cannot yet be submitted through this website; contact options will be added when they are ready.
